Poacher Turned Diver: Poachers who turned their lives around.

By: Michael Duffett | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Just give a person a chance!

Unique Selling Point:
This is the uplifting story of a group of men in Houtbay who were poachers and had regular run ins with the police -Cape Town – “When you live in Hout Bay, it’s hard not to be a poacher. Because that is our main source of income - the sea.” Houtbay has scene it's share drama:“We were protesting for service delivery and access to the ocean, because once you are a poacher, you will never get a licence to go catch legally because you’ve got a criminal record. Maybe 90% of the people who fish in Hout Bay did not have legal rights,” he said.

“So we go at night, in dangerous conditions, when the water is rough, when the cops are not on the water. I’ve lost a couple of people at sea,”
So said Angelo Joseph, the community liaison officer for a project under the umbrella of the Department of Public Works’ Small Harbours Rescue initiative, where a group of former Hout Bay poachers have changed their lives by becoming trained and accredited commercial divers.

Operation Phakisa focuses on unlocking the economic potential of South Africa's oceans, which could contribute up to R177 billion to the GDP by 2033. Many harbours were identified in the Cape as having fallen into disrepute and one of them was Houtbay where over 30 boats had been sunk in the harbour. These fishing harbours around the Cape needed to be brought back to good standing to attract more private investments and of course increase their tourist potential.

Summary:
Houtbay has been a bit of a hot spot in terms of poaching and we have doing a story on this before - which can form some context. Annaliesa did the story in 2018. A man like Stephan Braaf grew up in Houtbay and his family lived off the sea. When his grand parents died, he then started poaching to make a living for his gamily. And so did many others. In a really proactive way, the Dept of Public works set aside money for about 12 poachers to be trained as professional divers. It changed their lives - and they were all used by one major company in the area to revamp Houtbay - so many fishing vessels to lift from the ocean in the Harbour. And these men were used also to clean up other harbours .

Further information:
Stephen Braaf even went on to form his own diving company with another one of the ex poachers. I have met a few of the men - and Stephan is amazing. We can have access to amazing drone footage of other harbours where they have done work.
It's a simple story of what happens when you give people a chance. it's inspiring - from being arrested for poaching - living a life of trying to dodge the police - to now being a professional diver and being part owner of a company. In the story we feature some of the divers, Govt person who initiated the idea to use poachers, head if the dive school that trained the men -
I believe that the personal stories will be rich

Script:


Promo 1

upsound: From poacher to commercial fiver – what caused the transformation?
Promo 2
Dangerous and illegal – but the proceeds made from poaching abalone are so lucrative that poachers will risk it all – so why did one poacher convert and become a certificated commercial diver instead.
Promo 3
Just how did a national government decision to revamp fishing harbours in the western cape turn a well know abalone poacher into a certified commercial diver and business owner.

SCRIPT

Fully laden with his diving dear, 34 year old Stephan Braaf ambles his way down from his home in Hangberg to Houtbay Harbour. Sometimes he still reflects on the life he has left behind.

PRESENTER:
For 3 years Stephan was a full time poacher dodging the police as he plied his trade – it was a difficult and dangerous job, but it bought in the money to support his family.

Stehpan, a skilled diver in his youth, still remembers the time when his grandfather passed away. (SENT PIC)

Stephan: because he spoke to me on his death bed – that you must look after your grand mother.

16 at the time, stephan felt that he had no option but to start poaching. After getting his matric , full time poaching became his way of life to support himself and family members.

Stephan: So I went full time into the black operation, as they say..
Derek: Black operation, which is proper poaching.
Stephan: it's proper poaching as they call it.

LINK: hangberg, the community above HOUTBAY has struggled financially for decades. Looking out over the Atlantic ocean some residents has seen marine poaching as a way to pay the bills

Dwindling fish stocks, resulting in the government limiting fishing quotas combined with the high levels of unemployment meant that many traditional fisherman turned to CRAYFISH, lobster and ABOLIONE POACHING, . 24 year old Nevan adonis who lives with his grand mother , mother, girl friend and other family members comes from a long line of poachers.

Adonis: INTERVIEW

From a young age Neven was keen swimmer but as he grew older, he carried on the family tradition . (PLEASE IMPROVE SENTENCE)

Adonis;:Only issue is to be not caught by the police.
Derek: Never caught?
Addonis: Never..
Derek: How come, too clever?
Adonis; no, just never was..

Stephan wasn't so lucky, twice he was arrested for abaloine poaching - once off Ribbon island but the risk was worth it.

Derek: let's talk money, how much?
Stephan: 20. 000 per day.

But it came at a cost – poaching is dangerous work.

Stephan: I have list friends, never found them......

LINK: Then a life line was thrown to these poachers... it came in the form of the national dept's allocation of funs to revamp harbours in the western cape.

Over 400 million rand was assigned to the small harbours development project – 12 harbour in the western province including Houtbay, needed repairs. For example many vessels had sunk in the harbour and needed to be lifted out of the water. Mustakim Gierdien from National Dept of public works has overseen the project since 2017.

Gierdien: And in this harbour there were 15 so we needed to look at poachers and turning their lives around as well as removing the sunken vessels - from an area they were very familiar with:

DEREK: How do you look for poachers, they are not exactly on a recruitment agency list:

Gierdien: So what we do is we enage with every community where we look proclaimed harbour is to be found and we look at the leadership.

Please fix below
GUERRINI MARINE CONSTRUCTION who was awarded the contract for Houtbay, used over a 3rd of their budget for job creation.. . It was Houtbay Businessman Angelo Joesph who pushed the idea of using poachers,

Angelo: We had a meeting with the contractor , I said you have to train 10 poachers from the community – to become commercial divers, that is one of our cries in the community, for people to become commercial divers.

In the end 9 divers (XXXXXXX) were selected of which 5 were poachers Neven and Stephan included.


Stephan: That was the moment my life changed...from abalone to this new venture.

The task of turning these poachers into certified commercial divers fell to Trevor Bailey,, and his team. The course was two months long and he had no doubt that they would make the cut.

Trevor: I mean these are guts who ae used to swimming from robben island. 7, 8 k's every day - these are guys that ha be beeb left at sea, very competent guys, comptepant divers, copment people, but with no accreditation, no qualifications, to support that.

These newly qualified commercial divers worked alongside the main contractors divers - the operation to lift out sunken vessels took over 6 months, months. It was gruelling work - the divers were required to drill into sunken vessels and attach rigging . But It was work that Stephan relished.

Stephan: I was so excited at first, I could not sleep at night, I was just thinjkinh, I need to get to site, if its 7 am, then I am here 6am

It was in saldahna bay in another operation to remove sunken vessels that commercial diver Jerraau fraser who has spent long stints working on oil rigs, met Stephan. He was immediately impressed:

Jerraur: You should see how he works -

Jeaaur had just started his own commercial diving company and he asked Stephan to become a partner. - they began doing sub contract work , and at the beginning of lock down down , they and their management team set up headquarters in Montague gardens

When we met the team in Houtbay, , they were preparing to do underwater inspections for work they had just recently completed. Getting ready for a dive takes time and any short cuts can PROVE deadly. Helping Stephan was Nevan who also has been employed by the company. Once coms had been established, it IT WAS TIME FOR STEPHAN TO GET INTO THE WAYTER



HANDS THE KNIFE.

On standby ….Nevan - in case Stephan ran into problems. He's only too happy to have left his previous life behind

Adonis: I am happy to leave behind old life, I have learnt so much, I pushed myself myself, its a dream.

And Stephan's dream' is for poachers can get the same opportunity that was afford to him …...because he knows the perils of poaching.
